vision.name: Marble Jar
vision.tagline: Every finished task, a marble in the jar. Every jar, a story you can tell your team.
vision.description: Marble Jar is the missing middle layer between agent observability and team communication tools. It gives every completed unit of agent work a visual, countable representation (a 'marble'), captured via a dead-simple SDK/MCP/REST/webhook call, with full trace lineage linked to Arize Phoenix. Marbles flow into a live, animated queue where humans review and dispatch updates—one-click or via automated rules—to the tools teams actually use (Jira, Slack, Teams, custom webhooks), all executed on-behalf-of the user for full auditability. Marbles can be grouped into Objectives for cost/time/token rollups and aggregate reporting.
goals: Provide a zero-friction, framework-agnostic way for agents to self-report completed work (agents.md, SDK, MCP, REST/webhook)
Create a consistent 'unit of work' concept (the marble) that bridges agent traces and human-facing status updates
Deliver a live, visual, satisfying queue that makes agent activity legible to non-technical stakeholders
Enable human-in-the-loop dispatch to Jira/Teams/Slack/webhooks, with a graduated path to rules-based automation
Ensure all downstream actions are performed on-behalf-of (OBO) the actual user for full audit trail and trust
Link deeply to Arize Phoenix for trace-level debugging without duplicating trace storage
Support rollups of marbles into Objectives for cost/time/token tracking and aggregate reporting
Expose a monitoring MCP so agents/dashboards can query jar and objective status programmatically
Scale ingestion and dispatch independently to handle thousands of concurrent agent events
target_users: Engineering teams running agent harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph, AutoGen, custom pipelines)
Engineering managers and PMs who need visibility into agent-driven work without reading raw traces
Platform/DevOps teams responsible for agent observability and integration tooling
Organizations requiring auditable, identity-attributed actions from autonomous agents
Teams currently stuck between full-auto (untrusted) agents and fully manual status reporting
vision.problem_statement: There is a significant gap between an AI agent completing work and a team actually knowing about and trusting that it happened. Agent traces are scattered across disconnected observability tools, there's no consistent unit-of-work concept, and no reliable bridge connects agent completions to the tools teams rely on (Jira, Slack, Teams). This forces organizations to choose between full-auto agents they don't trust or fully manual status updates that negate the benefits of delegation.
success_metrics: Number of marbles logged per day/week across active workspaces
Time from agent task completion to marble dispatch/team notification
Percentage of marbles handled via automated rules vs. manual dispatch
Adoption across integration on-ramps (agents.md, SDK, MCP, webhook)
Reduction in manual status-update overhead reported by teams
Number of active Objectives and rollup reports generated
System throughput/latency under concurrent event load (ingestion + WS fanout)
User trust/adoption curve from manual dispatch to automated rules over time

services.name: marble_jar_core
services.description: The primary Marble Jar backend: a modular monolith handling marble ingestion, the real-time WebSocket queue, REST API for the frontend and SDKs, objectives, rules engine, and OBO token-exchange orchestration. Internally organized into clear packages (ingest, ws, objectives, rules, auth) but deployed as a single service to minimize operational overhead.
responsibilities: Expose REST API for logging marbles (log_marble equivalent over HTTP), fetching jar/queue state, objectives, and audit history
Accept high-throughput marble events and publish them to Redpanda for durable fan-out
Run the WebSocket gateway that pushes live marble events to connected frontend clients via Redis pub/sub
Manage Objectives: grouping marbles, computing cost/time/token rollups, progress tracking, and 'ship it' aggregate summary generation
Implement the rules engine that evaluates conditions (e.g., project=payments-api) and triggers auto-dispatch to integration workers
Orchestrate OBO (on-behalf-of) token exchange with Ory Hydra/Kratos (or Auth0) for Jira/Teams/Slack scoped actions
Store and query marble/objective/audit data in PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB, including JSONB metadata and time-series cost/token trend queries
Enforce authentication/authorization for SDK, MCP bridge, and frontend clients
Serve as the single source of truth service that the frontend, SDKs, and MCP bridge all talk to

Record dispatch outcomes (success/failure, external ticket/message IDs) back to marble_jar_core for audit trail
Refresh/use short-lived OBO tokens obtained via token exchange for each outbound call

db_schema.raw_sql:
-- Marble Jar full database migration
-- Requires pgcrypto for gen_random_uuid()
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;

-- ==================== auth_service ====================

CREATE TABLE organizations (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    slug TEXT NOT NULL,
    settings JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_organizations_slug ON organizations (slug);

CREATE TABLE users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    email TEXT NOT NULL,
    display_name TEXT,
    avatar_url TEXT,
    role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
    is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_organization_id ON users (organization_id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email);

CREATE TABLE api_keys (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    key_prefix TEXT NOT NULL,
    hashed_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    scopes TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_api_keys_organization_id ON api_keys (organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_api_keys_key_prefix ON api_keys (key_prefix);

CREATE TABLE oauth_connections (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    provider TEXT NOT NULL,
    provider_account_id TEXT,
    access_token_encrypted TEXT NOT NULL,
    refresh_token_encrypted TEXT,
    scopes TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_oauth_connections_org_provider ON oauth_connections (organization_id, provider);
CREATE INDEX idx_oauth_connections_user_id ON oauth_connections (user_id);

CREATE TABLE obo_audit_log (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    acting_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    agent_identity TEXT,
    provider TEXT NOT NULL,
    action TEXT NOT NULL,
    marble_id UUID,
    dispatch_id UUID,
    details JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_obo_audit_log_org_id ON obo_audit_log (organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_obo_audit_log_marble_id ON obo_audit_log (marble_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_obo_audit_log_created_at ON obo_audit_log (created_at);

-- ==================== core_api ====================

CREATE TABLE projects (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    slug TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_projects_organization_id ON projects (organization_id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_projects_org_slug ON projects (organization_id, slug);

CREATE TABLE agents (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    harness TEXT,
    default_model TEXT,
    metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_agents_organization_id ON agents (organization_id);

CREATE TABLE objectives (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    project_id UUID REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
    created_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    budget_tokens BIGINT,
    budget_cost_usd NUMERIC(12,4),
    shipped_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_objectives_organization_id ON objectives (organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_objectives_project_id ON objectives (project_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_objectives_status ON objectives (status);

CREATE TABLE marbles (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    project_id UUID REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    objective_id UUID REFERENCES objectives(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    agent_id UUID REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    created_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    summary TEXT NOT NULL,
    model TEXT,
    tokens_in INTEGER,
    tokens_out INTEGER,
    cost_usd NUMERIC(12,6),
    duration_ms INTEGER,
    trace_id TEXT,
    phoenix_trace_url TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'logged',
    metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sdk',
    occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_marbles_organization_id ON marbles (organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_marbles_project_id ON marbles (project_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_marbles_objective_id ON marbles (objective_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_marbles_agent_id ON marbles (agent_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_marbles_occurred_at ON marbles (occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_marbles_trace_id ON marbles (trace_id);

CREATE TABLE dispatch_rules (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    project_id UUID REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    condition JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    target_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    target_config JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_dispatch_rules_organization_id ON dispatch_rules (organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_dispatch_rules_project_id ON dispatch_rules (project_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_dispatch_rules_target_type ON dispatch_rules (target_type);

CREATE TABLE dispatches (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    organization_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    marble_id UUID REFERENCES marbles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    objective_id UUID REFERENCES objectives(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    dispatch_rule_id UUID REFERENCES dispatch_rules(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    integration_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    action TEXT NOT NULL,
    acting_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    request_payload JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    response_payload JSONB,
    external_ref TEXT,
    error_message TEXT,
    attempt_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    dispatched_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_dispatches_organization_id ON dispatches (organization_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_dispatches_marble_id ON dispatches (marble_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_dispatches_objective_id ON dispatches (objective_id);

CREATE TABLE marble_events (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

    marble_id UUID REFERENCES marbles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

frontend.design_notes:
Marble Jar's frontend should feel like a living, tactile product — not a dashboard you tolerate but one you *want* to glance at. The brand moment is the physical jar: marbles literally drop, roll, and settle with matter.js physics whenever a new completed unit of work arrives via WebSocket. This isn't decoration — it's the primary at-a-glance signal of "is my team of agents shipping right now."

Visual language: warm, glassy, tactile — think frosted glass jar cards on a soft neutral (off-white/graphite dark-mode) canvas, with marble colors mapped semantically (color = model or project, size = relative cost/duration, subtle glow = high-token-cost outlier). Typography is clean and confident (Inter/Geist), data-dense where it needs to be (trace/cost tables) but never cluttered — generous whitespace around the jar itself so the animation has room to breathe. Dark mode is first-class since this lives on a second monitor / TV in an eng bullpen.

Layout pattern: persistent left sidebar (workspace switcher, nav: Queue, Objectives, Rules, Integrations, Settings) + top bar (live connection status pill, quick-filter, user/OBO identity badge). Main content area is a responsive grid — the Live Queue page is the flagship view with the animated jar canvas pinned top-center/hero and a real-time scrollable marble list/table beneath or beside it for the data-dense crowd who wants specifics without waiting for animation.

Core interaction patterns:
- Every marble is clickable → slides in a right-side Sheet/drawer with full trace lineage (deep link to Phoenix), cost/token/duration breakdown, dispatch actions (Create Jira / Update Jira / Post Teams / Post Slack / Webhook), and OBO identity used.
- Objectives are drag-and-drop targets: drag marbles from the queue onto an objective card to bucket them, with an animated 'marble rolls into jar' transition. Objective detail page shows rollup progress bars (cost/time/tokens vs optional budget), a marble list, and a prominent 'Ship It' button that triggers the aggregate-summary dispatch flow with a preview/confirm modal.
- Rules engine is a lightweight visual builder (condition chips: project/model/cost-threshold → action: Slack/Teams/Jira/webhook) with a table of existing rules and a live 'test against last 20 marbles' preview.
- Empty/zero states matter a lot here — an empty jar should look inviting (soft pulsing 'waiting for your first marble' animation), not broken.

State management: Zustand for local/UI state (jar animation queue, sheet/drawer open state, filters, workspace context, OBO identity, WS connection status) kept deliberately thin. TanStack Query owns all server state (marbles, objectives, rules) with WebSocket events used to surgically patch the query cache (setQueryData) rather than duplicating server state in Zustand — this keeps optimistic updates, retries, and pagination consistent while the socket just supplies the 'push' half of the experience.

Libraries: shadcn/ui + Tailwind for component primitives (Sheet, Dialog, Command palette, DataTable via TanStack Table), Radix underneath for accessibility, TanStack Query for server cache + polling fallback if WS drops, native WebSocket client wrapped in a small reconnecting hook, matter.js for the jar physics canvas, Framer Motion for micro-interactions (drawer transitions, marble-drag-to-objective, rule builder chip animations), react-hook-form + zod for all forms (marble filters, objective creation, rule builder), date-fns for relative timestamps, recharts for cost/token/time trend sparklines on Objective and Analytics views.

Overall the product should read as: confident, playful without being juvenile, and fast — the queue must feel instantaneous and alive, because the entire pitch is turning invisible agent labor into something legible and satisfying to watch.

sdk.auth_pattern: Bearer token auth. The SDK is instantiated with an in-memory TokenStore (access token + optional refresh token). All authenticated requests attach `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. On a 401 response, the SDK's internal HttpClient will attempt exactly one silent refresh via AuthClient.refreshToken() (if a refresh token is present), retry the original request once, and otherwise throw an AuthError. Tokens are never persisted to localStorage by the SDK itself — consumers may plug in a custom TokenStore (e.g. backed by cookies/secure storage) via MarbleJarClientConfig.tokenStore. OBO (on-behalf-of) tokens for integrations (Jira/Teams/Slack) are fetched on demand via AuthClient.exchangeObo() and cached in memory per integration with expiry tracking.
sdk.base_url_config: MarbleJarClientConfig accepts a `baseUrl` (default: process.env.MARBLE_JAR_API_URL or 'https://api.marblejar.app') plus optional per-service overrides (`coreApiUrl`, `authApiUrl`, `ingestionApiUrl`) since core_api, auth_service, and ingestion_api may be deployed on distinct hosts. All dispatch worker dead-letter/replay endpoints and webhook-endpoint management are assumed to be proxied through core_api's base URL under distinct route prefixes (/v1/dead-letters/jira, /teams, /slack, /webhook) unless explicit worker URLs are supplied via `workerUrls` map.

adrs.title: Event-driven backbone (Redpanda/Kafka API) decoupling ingestion from persistence and dispatch
adrs.context: Marble Jar must accept high-throughput 'log_marble' events from many concurrent agent harnesses (SDK, MCP, webhook) while also fanning out to: (a) a live WebSocket queue, (b) durable persistence in core_api/Postgres, and (c) multiple independent integration dispatch workers (Jira, Teams, Slack, webhook). Coupling ingestion synchronously to all downstream consumers would create tight latency dependencies, cascading failures, and scaling bottlenecks — e.g. a slow Jira API would block marble ingestion.
adrs.decision: Use Redpanda (Kafka-compatible API) as the central event backbone. ingestion_api publishes normalized 'marble.logged' and 'dispatch.intent' events to topics; core_api, phoenix_bridge, and the four dispatch workers consume independently. Redis pub/sub is used only for the ephemeral, low-latency WS fanout to the frontend, not for durable event storage.
adrs.rationale: Kafka-API semantics give us durable, replayable, ordered-per-key event logs which are essential for audit trail correctness and for allowing new consumers (e.g. future integrations, analytics) to be added without touching ingestion_api. Redpanda specifically avoids JVM/ZooKeeper operational overhead while remaining wire-compatible with the Kafka ecosystem and client libraries our Go/Python services already target.
consequences: Ingestion latency is decoupled from dispatch/integration latency; a failing Jira API cannot back-pressure marble logging.
Consumers (core_api, dispatch workers, phoenix_bridge) can be scaled, restarted, or replayed independently using consumer groups and offsets.
Introduces operational complexity of running/monitoring a Redpanda cluster and managing topic schemas/versioning (recommend a shared schema registry or protobuf contracts).
Requires idempotent consumers (esp. dispatch workers, core_api rollups) since at-least-once delivery is expected.

Redis pub/sub remains a separate, non-durable channel purely for the WS live-queue feed; a WS client that reconnects may miss transient jar-animation events but not the durable marble record itself (backfilled via core_api REST on reconnect).

adrs.title: On-behalf-of (OBO) delegated auth via a dedicated auth_service fronting Ory Hydra/Kratos
adrs.context: Every downstream integration action (Jira issue creation, Teams post, Slack post, webhook) must be attributable to the actual human user, not a shared bot identity, for audit and trust reasons stated as a core product differentiator. This requires token exchange across multiple external OAuth providers (Atlassian, Entra ID, Slack) plus our own internal session/API auth, and dispatch workers must not each independently implement OAuth flows.
adrs.decision: Introduce a standalone auth_service (Go) that fronts Ory Hydra/Kratos (or Auth0) as the identity provider, implements OAuth2 token-exchange (RFC 8693-style) per integration, and exposes a single internal gRPC/REST interface for (1) verifying incoming user/API tokens and (2) minting short-lived, scoped OBO tokens for a given (user, integration) pair on demand. Dispatch workers call auth_service rather than talking to Atlassian/Entra/Slack OAuth endpoints directly.
adrs.rationale: Centralizing OBO logic in one service keeps OAuth credential handling, refresh logic, and scope management standards-based and auditable in a single place, avoids duplicating fragile OAuth code across four dispatch workers, and gives us one place to enforce token expiry/revocation and log 'who acted as whom' for compliance.
consequences: All dispatch workers take a hard dependency on auth_service being available and low-latency; requires caching of short-lived tokens within workers plus circuit breakers/backoff if auth_service is degraded.
Centralizes a single point of audit truth ('which agent, under whose identity, did what') which directly satisfies the product's OBO-first trust requirement.
Adds an extra network hop for every dispatch action versus embedding OAuth clients per worker; acceptable given dispatch is not on the hot ingestion path.

Requires secure storage (e.g. encrypted at rest, short TTL) of refresh tokens per user per integration, increasing the security surface that must be operated carefully (secrets rotation, breach containment).

adrs.title: PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB as the single system of record; Phoenix remains the trace store (thin pointer layer)
adrs.context: Marble Jar needs relational integrity for marbles/objectives/rules/audit (structured entities with foreign keys and ACID guarantees for dispatch/audit correctness), plus efficient time-series rollups for cost/token/duration trends across objectives. Arize Phoenix already provides OTel/OpenInference-native trace storage; duplicating full trace data in Marble Jar's own store would be redundant, expensive, and would compete with a best-of-breed tool.
adrs.decision: Use PostgreSQL with the TimescaleDB extension as core_api's sole primary datastore, storing marbles, objectives, rules-engine config, audit trail as relational rows plus JSONB metadata, and using Timescale hypertables for cost/token/duration trend queries. Marble Jar stores only a trace_id pointer plus rollup metrics (cost, duration, token counts) per marble/objective; phoenix_bridge is responsible for enriching those rollups by querying Phoenix, never for replicating full trace payloads.
adrs.rationale: This keeps Marble Jar's data model lean and avoids building/maintaining a second trace-storage system, while TimescaleDB gives us the time-series query performance needed for objective cost/time dashboards without introducing a separate analytics database. JSONB gives schema flexibility for heterogeneous agent/model metadata without a migration per new agent framework.
consequences: Marble Jar is architecturally dependent on Phoenix's availability and API stability for any deep trace drill-down; an outage in Phoenix degrades trace links but not core marble/objective functionality (rollups already cached in Postgres).
phoenix_bridge must handle eventual consistency — rollups may lag briefly behind trace ingestion into Phoenix — and needs its own retry/backfill logic.

Single Postgres/Timescale instance (with read replicas as needed) simplifies operations versus a polyglot persistence approach, but means core_api's DB is a scaling and availability bottleneck to monitor closely as event volume grows.
Schema/version changes to JSONB metadata fields must be handled defensively in application code since Postgres won't enforce their internal structure.

adrs.title: Polyglot services split by workload shape: Go for hot-path/concurrency, Python for MCP/Phoenix ecosystem
adrs.context: The system has two distinct workload classes: (1) high-throughput, low-latency, highly concurrent I/O — ingestion, WS fanout, integration dispatch — and (2) ecosystem-constrained integration work — MCP servers (official SDK is Python-first) and Phoenix/OpenInference trace enrichment, where Python is the idiomatic and best-supported client ecosystem.
adrs.decision: Implement ingestion_api, core_api, auth_service, and all four dispatch workers in Go. Implement mcp_log_marble_server, mcp_monitor_server, and phoenix_bridge in Python using the official MCP SDK and OpenInference/OTel exporters.
adrs.rationale: Go's goroutine-based concurrency and low memory footprint fit the thousands-of-concurrent-connections ingestion/dispatch workload well, while Python is mandated in practice by the MCP SDK and Phoenix/OpenInference ecosystem being Python-native — fighting that would mean reimplementing instrumentation that already exists idiomatically in Python.
consequences: Team must maintain cross-language conventions (shared event schemas via protobuf/JSON Schema, consistent structured logging/OTel instrumentation) to keep the two runtimes interoperable and observable as one system.
Requires two sets of CI/build/deploy tooling (Go modules + Python packaging) and two language-specific on-call skillsets, increasing operational overhead versus a single-language stack.
Enables independent scaling: Go services can be scaled aggressively for throughput while Python MCP/bridge services scale based on agent query/enrichment volume, which is typically much lower.

Client SDKs (TS/Python) and the mcp_log_marble_server all ultimately funnel into the same ingestion_api REST contract, keeping the polyglot boundary clean and limited to well-defined HTTP/event interfaces.

adrs.title: Dispatch-intent fan-out with per-integration worker isolation and HMAC-signed outbound payloads
adrs.context: Human-in-the-loop and rules-engine dispatch can target Jira, Teams, Slack, or arbitrary user webhooks. Each integration has different rate limits, failure modes, and external API stability. A single shared dispatch service would mean one integration's outage or bug (e.g. Jira rate-limiting) could delay or break delivery to unrelated integrations (e.g. Slack), and a bug in webhook signing logic could affect all integrations at once.
adrs.decision: core_api publishes a generic 'dispatch.intent' event (with target integration type, OBO subject, and payload) to Redpanda after a marble is manually dispatched or a rule fires. Each integration (jira_dispatch_worker, teams_dispatch_worker, slack_dispatch_worker, webhook_dispatch_worker) is a separately deployed Go service consuming only its relevant intent events, independently implementing retry/backoff, and signing outbound webhook payloads with HMAC where applicable.
adrs.rationale: Isolating blast radius per integration means one integration's degradation doesn't affect others, and each worker can be scaled, deployed, and rate-limited according to its own external API's characteristics (e.g. Jira's stricter rate limits vs Slack's).
consequences: Adds operational surface of four independently deployed/scaled services instead of one monolithic dispatcher, requiring consistent shared libraries for retry/backoff and OBO token usage to avoid logic drift.
Failure and retry state per integration must be independently observable (metrics/alerts per worker) so a stuck Jira queue is diagnosed separately from a stuck Slack queue.

New integrations can be added by writing a new consumer of 'dispatch.intent' without modifying core_api or existing workers, directly supporting the product's 'meet agents/teams where they are' extensibility goal.
Requires careful event schema versioning on 'dispatch.intent' since it is a shared contract consumed by multiple independently-deployed workers.

architecture.system_diagram_description: Agent harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph/AutoGen, custom) interact with Marble Jar via three on-ramps: direct REST/SDK calls, the mcp_log_marble_server (Python, MCP tool 'log_marble'), or generic webhooks — all converging on ingestion_api (Go). ingestion_api validates payloads, publishes 'marble.logged' events to the Redpanda event backbone, and also publishes ephemeral updates to Redis pub/sub, which it reads back from to drive a live WebSocket feed consumed by the React/TypeScript frontend (rendering the animated matter.js jar). From Redpanda, core_api (Go) consumes 'marble.logged' events, persists marbles/objectives/audit records into PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB, and exposes REST CRUD/query APIs (marbles, objectives, rules engine config) back to the frontend and to mcp_monitor_server (Python), which lets external agents/dashboards query jar status and cost/token trends. phoenix_bridge (Python) also consumes marble events (or polls core_api), queries Arize Phoenix for trace-derived cost/timing/token rollups, and writes those rollups back into Postgres via core_api, keeping Phoenix as the authoritative trace store and Marble Jar as a thin pointer layer. When a marble is manually dispatched from the frontend or a rule fires in core_api, a 'dispatch.intent' event is published to Redpanda, targeting one of four independently deployed Go workers — jira_dispatch_worker, teams_dispatch_worker, slack_dispatch_worker, webhook_dispatch_worker — each of which calls auth_service (Go) to obtain a short-lived OBO token (auth_service itself fronting Ory Hydra/Kratos and exchanging tokens with Atlassian OAuth, Entra ID, and Slack OAuth respectively), then performs the integration action (create/update Jira issue, post to Teams, post to Slack, fire HMAC-signed webhook) with its own retry/backoff logic. All services emit OpenTelemetry data to a self-observability stack (Grafana/Loki/Tempo), separate from the agent-facing Arize Phoenix trace store, and the whole system runs on Kubernetes deployed via Helm/ArgoCD from GitHub Actions CI/CD.

infrastructure.scaling_notes: marble_jar_core and marble_jar_dispatch_worker are Go services designed for high-concurrency, low-memory footprints — scale horizontally via K8s HPA based on CPU/goroutine-derived custom metrics and Redpanda consumer lag. marble_jar_mcp_bridge (Python) is likely lower-throughput (bridging MCP protocol/trace export) and can scale independently with fewer replicas, though Python GIL constraints mean scaling should favor horizontal pod replication over per-pod concurrency. Redpanda partitions should be sized to match ingestion parallelism and dispatch worker consumer group size. Redis pub/sub for WebSocket fanout should be monitored for connection/memory limits and may need Redis Cluster mode at high fanout scale. PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB should use read replicas for rollup queries and hypertable partitioning for time-series growth. Phoenix trace store scales independently since Marble Jar only stores pointers/rollups.
